title: Go after superhuman AI: evidence ledger
scope: Competitive Go; professional-game studies separated from online player experience.
method: Source inspection and qualitative synthesis. Original datasets, regression estimates, and supplementary analyses were not independently reproduced.

claims.claim: Brown posted that human Go skill improved after AlphaGo.
claims.locator: Main post; May 28, 2026
claims.limitation: Not an independent empirical study
claims.status: Post text and author verified in browser

claims.claim: Brown's attached chart measures yearly effects on decision quality, not rankings.
claims.locator: Figure 1A; PDF p.6, adjacent results p.5
claims.measurement: Year fixed effect on median decision-quality indices; player fixed effects; 1950 baseline; 95% confidence intervals
claims.limitation: First 60 moves; engine-evaluated proxy. Figure visually matched; no digitization or reanalysis
claims.status: Verified caption and attached chart

claims.claim: Brown's source reply links a Karlsson article that is now unavailable at the supplied path.
claims.locator: Source reply and redirected page-not-found screen
claims.limitation: Intermediary article content remains unverified
claims.status: Reply and unavailable destination verified in browser

claims.claim: Nagaraj emphasizes stronger effects among younger players and links Choi et al.
claims.locator: May 28, 2026 reply and paper link
claims.population: Professional players discussed by linked study
claims.limitation: Not a separate experiment; reply discussion is login-limited
claims.status: Verified in browser

claims.claim: Shin et al. report improved engine-evaluated decision quality and increased sequence novelty after the AI transition.
claims.locator: Abstract, Results, Figure 1, footnote on PDF p.7
claims.population: Professional Go decisions, 1950–2021; over 5.8 million moves
claims.measurement: KataGo-derived decision quality and historically novel sequences; first 60 moves
claims.limitation: Opening-window scope; historical comparison is not randomized AI access; does not measure enjoyment
claims.status: Main paper inspected; estimates not reproduced

claims.claim: Shin et al. test memorization explanations in multiple ways.
claims.locator: PDF pp.10–16
claims.measurement: Deviations from AI choices, later opening subsets, opponent deviations, inserted simulated AI sequences
claims.limitation: Main-text descriptions checked; supplemental figures and analysis code not independently reproduced
claims.status: Verified as reported tests, not as a conclusive exclusion of every memorization mechanism

claims.claim: Choi et al. report move-quality improvement, with stronger effects for younger professionals.
claims.locator: Abstract; §§3–5; research design around PDF pp.15–17
claims.measurement: Winning-probability difference from engine-preferred choices; main window first 30 moves
claims.limitation: No individual AI-use measure; older age group is not a clean untreated control; not an enjoyment study
claims.status: Verified as study finding; causal estimates not reproduced

claims.claim: The earlier study linked by the critic reports most measured improvement in early play.
claims.locator: Figure 2 and adjacent discussion, PDF pp.4–5
claims.measurement: Human–AI gap by ten-move bins; concentration of gains in moves 1–50
claims.limitation: Cannot prove absence of all later-game learning; arXiv version can differ from a cited earlier publication
claims.status: Stage result checked in linked PDF

claims.claim: TuesdayBornWhale challenges whether sequence novelty and engine agreement establish deeper understanding.
claims.locator: My critique; local joseki discussion; Appendix
claims.population: Professional-study interpretation and author's own competitive experience
claims.limitation: No representative sample or new controlled reanalysis
claims.status: Article inspected; interpretation labeled disputed

claims.claim: The critic reports deference to AI and an alleged online cheating example.
claims.locator: So… we aren't getting better?
claims.limitation: Individual allegation unverified; not used to establish cheating prevalence or accuse an identified individual
claims.status: Verified as author's reported experience only

claims.claim: PNAS Nexus reports new local opening patterns and greater concentration after AI access.
claims.locator: Methods and Results, PDF pp.2–5
claims.population: Professional games 2003–2021; full corpus 69,996 games; pattern analysis uses a subset
claims.measurement: Eight alternating moves in a quadrant; pattern shares, CR4, HHI
claims.limitation: No explicit counterfactual control group; diversity metric is not enjoyment
claims.status: Full-text copy inspected; publisher page intermittently inaccessible

claims.claim: The top ten patterns in 2021 accounted for 4.02% in 2003 and 66.8% in 2021 among the top skill decile; 2.48% and 52.6% among the bottom skill decile.
claims.locator: Figure 5 discussion, PDF p.4
claims.population: Top and bottom professional skill deciles
claims.measurement: Share of the set of ten patterns prominent in 2021, traced over time
claims.limitation: Not necessarily each year's own ten most frequent patterns; no enjoyment implication
claims.status: Values checked against full-text discussion; plotted on common 0–100% scale

claims.claim: Novelty and concentration findings need not contradict each other.
claims.locator: Novelty definition versus standard-pattern concentration definition
claims.measurement: Historical full sequence departure versus local pattern usage distribution
claims.limitation: Conceptual compatibility is not independent proof of either causal interpretation
claims.status: Inference explicitly distinguished from measured findings

claims.claim: OGS prohibits engine analysis of ongoing games unless permitted, and all outside help in live/blitz games.
claims.locator: No Cheating or Computer Help
claims.limitation: Does not measure prevalence, enforcement effectiveness, or enjoyment
claims.status: Current rendered policy checked in browser

claims.claim: Players have publicly raised fairness concerns about suspected live assistance.
claims.locator: Initial January 2021 post and replies
claims.limitation: Alleged cheating is not independently confirmed; sample not representative
claims.status: Source text inspected

claims.claim: Go teachers report both concerns and satisfaction about educational AI tools.
claims.locator: Journal abstract for Trinks & Oh, December 7, 2023
claims.limitation: Full survey methods not audited; teachers are not representative online competitors
claims.status: Verified abstract only; no competitive-enjoyment inference

claims.claim: Bessis distinguishes understanding and meaning from output production and challenges a mathematics–Go analogy.
claims.locator: Opening argument; The way of Go and Chess
claims.population: Mathematical community as discussed by author
claims.limitation: Does not empirically study Go experience; used only as a framing lens
claims.status: Essay inspected

claims.claim: Go AI has demonstrated superhuman strength and tested engines can have exploitable weaknesses.
claims.locator: Developer historical research account; adversarial project and study
claims.limitation: Not a current exhaustive best-engine ranking or proof that humans are generally superior
claims.status: Scope-qualified finding verified

claims.claim: The inspected evidence does not establish a population-wide reduction in online Go enjoyment or participation.
claims.source: Starting-source collection and supporting evidence listed above
claims.locator: Outcomes and populations in inspected sources
claims.measurement: No representative direct outcome estimate located in inspected material
claims.limitation: Not proof of no harm; not an exhaustive systematic review
claims.status: Supported as a bounded statement about inspected evidence

claims.claim: Training, review, practice, and live assistance may affect agency and fairness differently.
claims.locator: Use-setting comparison in brief
claims.limitation: Benefits and risks labeled potential where direct outcome evidence is absent
claims.status: Explicitly hypothetical where appropriate

claims.claim: The project reports Pelrine winning 14 of 15 games against JBXKata005 on KGS; a separate example exploits KataGo at 100,000 visits with network b18c384nbt-uec.
claims.locator: Human exploits a top KGS bot; Human exploits KataGo; game record tables
claims.population: One expert against specified historical bot implementations
claims.measurement: Recorded wins using learned cyclic exploits
claims.limitation: Hardware and complete time/rule conditions not stated in visible summary; not proof against the current best engine under arbitrary conditions
claims.status: Rendered primary research page and game tables checked in browser

visuals.name: Hero Go board
visuals.data: No recorded match or claimed outcome

visuals.name: Brown attached chart
visuals.data: Source image viewed in browser; figure/caption matched; not reconstructed

visuals.name: DQI calculator
visuals.data: Reader-controlled hypothetical probabilities; index=100-(best-human); not study measurements

x_coverage.brown_post: Inspected main text, author, displayed date, attached chart
x_coverage.embedded_quoted_post: Visible Gowers text in Brown's post read; mathematics context, not Go outcome evidence

No quote-post listing navigation available in inspected page; More menu exposes only Embed post. No authenticated access was used. Search did not supply verifiable additional quote posts.
